CVE-2026-128424.title: Kroxylicious-authorizer-acl: kroxylicious: acl rule file regex escapes are stripped, broadening 'matching' authorization rules
CVE-2026-128424.description: A flaw was found in Kroxylicious. The ACL authorizer's rules-file parser unquotes `matching /…/` regular-expression literals using the string unquoting rules, which strips every backslash escape. As a result, an allow rule such as `matching /orders\.v1/` is compiled as the regex `orders.v1`, which also matches unintended names such as `ordersXv1`, and character classes such as `\d` and `\w` lose their special meaning. Allow rules written with regex escapes can therefore apply to more resources than the author intended. Depending on the ACL configuration, this may allow an authenticated Kafka client to access a resource (such as read or write a topic) that should have been denied.

CVE-2026-15353.title: SOAP information disclosure through malformed array dimensions
CVE-2026-15353.description:
SOAP information disclosure through malformed array dimensions.

The SOAP extension reads an uninitialized array position when decoding an encoded array whose arraySize attribute is empty, whitespace-only or non-numeric, or when such dimensions come from a WSDL definition. Four bytes of unrelated heap data can then be used as an integer key in the decoded array. An unauthenticated remote client can trigger this with a crafted request to a SoapServer endpoint, and a malicious SOAP server with a response to SoapClient. Heap memory is disclosed only if the application returns or otherwise exposes the decoded array.

This issue affects PHP versions before 8.2.36, 8.3.* before 8.3.37, 8.4.* before 8.4.28 and 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

CVE-2026-99612.title: ALSA: hda/tas2781: Only accept CRC-less V1 data if all entries are valid
CVE-2026-99612.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ALSA: hda/tas2781: Only accept CRC-less V1 data if all entries are valid

Commit 408249089c48 ("ALSA: hda/tas2781: Accept V1 calibration data
without CRC") only checked the first device entry. On machines where
the BIOS populates fewer entries than p->ndev, the remaining all-zero
entries are applied and tas2781_cali_preproc() divides by zero on
playback open.

Accept CRC-less V1 data only if every expected entry is non-zero and
self-consistent (R0 * 1/R0 close to 1.0), otherwise reject it as
before.
